Random sampling counters automation bias by ensuring that not all investigations are based solely on high-risk signals generated by algorithms. By incorporating a random sample into the fraud detection process, inspectors are encouraged to critically evaluate cases rather than relying blindly on algorithmic results. This approach helps to monitor and mitigate risks of discrimination, as it allows for the tracking of whether certain groups are disproportionately represented in algorithmic outcomes.

Regarding the AI Act duties for high-risk providers, the use of random sampling aligns with the requirements for high-risk AI systems to identify and mitigate foreseeable risks, including potential discrimination. The AI Act mandates that providers of high-risk systems implement measures to ensure compliance with regulations, and random sampling can serve as a control tool to help fulfill these obligations by providing a means to assess and improve the fairness and effectiveness of the algorithms used.
